name: What is considered a brain injury in a personal injury claim?

mainEntity.name: What is considered a brain injury in a personal injury claim?

acceptedAnswer.text: In a personal injury claim, a brain injury can range from a mild concussion to a severe traumatic brain injury (TBI). It typically involves any injury to the brain caused by an external force, such as a blow to the head, a sudden jolt, or penetration. Symptoms can vary widely, including headaches, dizziness, memory problems, cognitive difficulties, and mood changes. The severity and long-term impact of the injury are key factors in a personal injury claim.
acceptedAnswer.description: A brain injury in a personal injury claim refers to any injury to the brain caused by an external force, from concussions to severe traumatic brain injuries. Symptoms and long-term effects are critical to the claim.
